entries.notes: countersubject proper from 2nd note of bar 9 in bass
interchange of first stretto; bar 38 cannot be played as written on one keyboard
starts as if answer, continues with subject intervals; alto imitates tenor
restores original length of opening note; alto and tenor imitative figures give illusion of taking part

episodes.name: episode
episodes.material: codetta figure, octave leaps of bars 12-13, figures from first part of subject; soprano followed by alto in canon at the fifth
episodes.sequence: suggests vi, ii, V, I before moving to IV

countersubjects.first: apparent CS starts with imitation of codetta figure; CS proper from 2nd note of bar 9 to end of answer at 12
countersubjects.interchange: interchangeable at the octave with subject, but never appears above subject or answer

subject.ends: disputed: simpler analysis ends it at first note of bar 7 (then only codettas are bars 13 and 20); but cadence feeling of bars 5-6 and the many 48 subjects ending on the mediant suggest it ends at bar 6, with a bar of codetta
subject.answer: tonal (2nd note, the dominant, answered by tonic at bar 8); rest in bars 2 and 8 'all-important'; without the tonal answer the three stretti would have been impossible

stretti.name: Stretto 1
stretti.notes: counterexposition in stretto instead of modulating episode; 'one of the most natural-sounding and harmonious partnerships' in the 48; from bar 33 two voices without supporting parts

stretti.name: Stretto 2
stretti.notes: interchange of stretto 1 with harmony added by lower voices

stretti.name: Stretto 3
stretti.notes: first stretto repeated 'with maximum effect' in final section

claims.claim: Subject length disputed: end at first note of bar 7 or at bar 6 (mediant ending, cadence feeling)
Tonal answer was necessary for the three stretti
Countersubject never appears above the subject/answer
Exposition occupies almost half the fugue; instead of modulating, a counterexposition in stretto follows
Single episode (43-53) compensates for extended use of I and V by suggesting vi, ii, V, I before IV
Tenor entry at 53 starts as answer but continues as subject, 'quite common'
